summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, peripheral vascular disease, and a history of bilateral below-knee amputations was admitted for a right lower extremity stump infection. She presented after a visiting nurse noted poor wound healing and purulent discharge. She was hypertensive on admission and started on hydralazine. A PICC line was placed for antibiotic administration. Hyponatremia developed and was corrected with saline. She underwent revision and debridement of the stump due to infection, with intraoperative findings of necrotic tissue. MRSA was identified, and she was treated with ciprofloxacin. Postoperatively, pain was managed with a PCA pump, then transitioned to oral opioids. Physical therapy initiated rehabilitation. Her condition stabilized, and she was discharged to an extended care facility with a two-week course of antibiotics, wound care instructions, and follow-up planned in three weeks for suture removal.
